doc.title: Types
doc.paragraph: Adaptive Script can annotate variables, function parameters and returns, and local type names with Adaptive data types and simple structured types. Leaves are the registered data types such as integer, string, boolean, object, array, any, and void.

These annotations are part of the script language. They are separate from adaptive object types and property meta used by adapters and requests. Object-type rules at the adapter and request layer are unchanged. Script type and interface declarations define shapes used only for script type checking.
T[] and Array<T> describe the same array type. Optional properties use ?. Unions use |; intersections use &. Function types use (parameters) => Return.
Type annotations are always accepted by the compiler. Checking is off by default so existing scripts keep working. Turn checking on with environment flags when you want mismatches reported.

list.item: compile:typeCheck — checks at compile time when the right-hand side type is known, and at runtime on assignment and script function parameters.
compile:typeCheckCompileOnly — compile-time checks only (used instead of full typeCheck when both are set).
compile:noImplicitAny — when checking is active, a missing annotation is an error instead of any.
compile:strictNullChecks — stricter handling of null and undefined.
compile:strict — turns on typeCheck, noImplicitAny, and strictNullChecks together.

doc.paragraph: Flags may be set from the host environment or with flag_set in a script. When compile checking is on, calls to known Adaptive functions are also checked at compile time against each function’s parameter and return data types (when those types can be determined without running the call).

list.item: Data type leaves (for example integer versus string).
Array types: the value must be an array; element types are checked when the value is known (for example an array literal).
Tuples: length and each position when the value is known.

Object and interface shapes: required properties must be present; property values must match their types; extends bases are included. An object literal may not include properties outside the type (including when used as a function argument). Object literals with spreads or computed property names skip that extra-key check. At runtime, extra properties on an already-evaluated value are still allowed so adaptive objects can be wider than the script type.
Function return types when a return type is declared.
Function types: script functions and closures are checked for parameter and return compatibility; other function values only need data type function.
List and object patterns: binding annotations such as const [a: integer] = … or { host: h: string } are enforced when checking is on.

doc.paragraph: Bindings without an annotation, and data that arrives from outside the script, are treated as any at compile time unless noImplicitAny is set. Runtime data type and adaptive object-type rules still apply on their own.
